speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; please describe exactly what happens when you feel dizzy, such as whether the room spins or you feel faint, and if you have any accompanying symptoms like hearing loss, nausea, or double vision.

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The brief, spinning episode lasting only 3 minutes upon lying down, followed by resolution and current baseline status, is classic for BPPV. Given your age and the specific nature of the attack, this is likely a canalithiasis event in the posterior semicircular canal. I will not order further testing as the clinical presentation is diagnostic, but I would recommend a Brandt-Daroff exercise regimen.
